open_items: An interrupted preparation without a complete durable journal remains an untouched conflict; automatic cleanup cannot infer ownership from unverified remnants. Existing project edits invalidate init replay without deleting data. Journal consistency is not authentication of a deliberately reconstructed foreign record.
The native implementation is currently Linux/local-filesystem only; other platform, filesystem and complete release coverage remain open. Advisory mutexes do not sandbox noncooperating host writers.
Parent directories must already exist. Whole bootstrap inputs and inventory are memory-resident. Full later document/project semantic gates are not implemented by initialization.
18.v: fresh stage-specific Apply evidence is required. Dev only prepared the implementation, behavioral oracles and pure collection; no behavior tests ran in Dev.

oracle.requirement_contract: Der Befehl `specroad init [PATH]` MUSS in `PATH` oder im aktuellen Verzeichnis ein neues SpecRoad-Projekt mit der in dieser Spezifikation definierten Mindeststruktur einschließlich genau eines Primärspezifikationsdokuments erzeugen.
oracle.scope: Real root creation and validated prepared-journal replay on native Linux/local filesystems. Replay verifies the entire closed inventory, root/stage/reused identities, publication prefix, native configuration/document fields and exact distribution bytes before publication; no new project/document IDs or timestamps. A durable passive completion receipt preserves evidence through the final rename. Foreign files and unverifiable states are preserved. Existing W oracles remain unchanged. This is not full semantic validation, authentication of deliberately reconstructed foreign evidence, arbitrary pre-journal recovery, cross-platform or release approval. 18.v binds the replacement interruption/normal-completion oracles; old automatic-repair evidence is historical only. Further plan scopes and release acceptance remain separate.

preconditions: Owned temporary directories; native Linux descriptor-relative reads, inode flock and renameat2 no-replace publication. Built module/zipapp cases use actual independently built distribution bytes in fresh isolated processes.
Use only owned native test roots with actual backup/original evidence. No historical success record authorizes replay or restoration of a protected partial publication.
steps: Execute native init and bundle extraction on their allowed missing/existing targets; compare complete actual configuration, document, resources, bundle payload and retained foreign bytes.

Before durable protection, refuse invalid input/collision without target changes. After protection, preserve the actual partial bytes and ownership markers; never roll back, finish or reuse the interrupted target.

Kill a real isolated process at publication boundaries. Refuse all normal reentry, even when configuration is absent or target publication is already complete; an independently chosen permissible new root may be created.

Reject altered/incomplete marker pairs, mismatching owners, unsafe links and changed inputs or target inventory. Successful original completion removes only its own marker after full native verification; completed passive receipt reads never publish files.
